It means the bearing between the connecting rod and crankshaft has failed. Oil pressure loss is imminent. Driving for even a few minutes will destroy the crankshaft and potentially the entire engine block. In our 24,650 quote dataset, 87% of rod knock cases resulted in engine replacement because drivers continued running the engine after symptoms appeared. 1 Detonation Sounds like marbles rattling in a can - occurs under load. £60-£400 2 Rod knock Sounds like a heavy hammer hitting metal - occurs at idle, worsens with RPM. £800-£1,500 early 3 Active failure Crankshaft damage begins. Oil pressure drops. £1,500-£3,500 4 Catastrophic Block damaged - full engine replacement. £2,500-£10,000+ What people think vs reality The expensive mistake is assuming it is harmless “It's just a timing issue - I can drive it to the garage.” If it's rod knock, the bearing is already failing. Each revolution causes more damage. Driving even 1 mile turns an £800 repair into a £5,000+ replacement. “I'll add thicker oil to quieten it.” Thicker oil masks the noise briefly while continuing to destroy the bearing. You're silencing the symptom, not fixing the problem. “My car has done 100k miles; this is normal wear.” Rod knock is not normal at any mileage. It's a failure of the lubrication system or bearing material. “A mechanic can fix this with an engine flush.” Engine flushes do not fix mechanical bearing failure. At best, they clean the system; at worst, they accelerate failure. sections.heading: Rod knock is the most serious engine noise you can hear

blocks.text: A deep, rhythmic knock that increases with engine RPM is rod knock. It means the bearing between the connecting rod and crankshaft has failed. Oil pressure loss is imminent. Driving for even a few minutes will destroy the crankshaft and potentially the entire engine block.
In our 24,650 quote dataset, 87% of rod knock cases resulted in engine replacement because drivers continued running the engine after symptoms appeared.
Sounds like marbles rattling in a can - occurs under load.
Sounds like a heavy hammer hitting metal - occurs at idle, worsens with RPM.
Crankshaft damage begins. Oil pressure drops.

sections.heading: The expensive mistake is assuming it is harmless

blocks.text: “It's just a timing issue - I can drive it to the garage.”
If it's rod knock, the bearing is already failing. Each revolution causes more damage. Driving even 1 mile turns an £800 repair into a £5,000+ replacement.
“I'll add thicker oil to quieten it.”
Thicker oil masks the noise briefly while continuing to destroy the bearing. You're silencing the symptom, not fixing the problem.
“My car has done 100k miles; this is normal wear.”
Rod knock is not normal at any mileage. It's a failure of the lubrication system or bearing material.
“A mechanic can fix this with an engine flush.”
Engine flushes do not fix mechanical bearing failure. At best, they clean the system; at worst, they accelerate failure.

blocks.question: What's the difference between engine knocking and rattling?
blocks.answer: Knocking is a deep, rhythmic "thud" that increases with engine RPM. Rattling is a metallic, higher-pitched sound. Knocking indicates bearing failure - more serious.

blocks.question: Can low oil cause engine knocking?
blocks.answer: Yes. Low oil causes insufficient lubrication, leading to bearing wear and ultimately rod knock. Check your oil level immediately.

blocks.question: Is detonation the same as rod knock?
blocks.answer: No. Detonation sounds like marbles rattling and occurs under acceleration. Rod knock is a deep rhythmic knock at idle that worsens with RPM.
